bib.title: Demystifying Reinforcement Learning in Agentic Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Demystifying Reinforcement Learning in Agentic Reasoning", Zhaochen Yu*, Ling Yang*, Jiaru Zou, Shuicheng Yan, Mengdi Wang (NUS, UIUC, Princeton). arXiv:2510.11701v1 [cs.CL], 13 Oct 2025. Preprint, no venue. Code: Open-AgentRL; model DemyAgent-4B.
COVERAGE: 24 of 24 pages, 73,255 of 73,255 chars, including appendices A-B (prompts, partly truncated in my view of B.2, no results there) and references (skimmed). Figures are not readable from text, so their curves are known only through the prose.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. DemyAgent-4B (Qwen3-4B-RA-SFT + GRPO-TCR, eps_high=0.315, 30k RL set) matches or beats 14B/32B agents in agentic mode.
 number: AIME24 72.6, AIME25 70.0, GPQA-D 58.5, LCB-v6 26.8
 setup: code interpreter; temp 1.0, top_p 0.6, 16384 max response, 32 samples per problem; baselines: ReTool-32B 72.5/54.3, rStar2-Agent-14B 80.6/69.8/60.9, ARPO-7B 30.0/30.0/53.0/18.3, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 agentic 17.9/16.3/44.3/23.0. Baseline numbers appear copied from other papers; self-evaluated ones are starred. rStar2-Agent-14B beats it on AIME24 and GPQA. Seeds and runs: not stated, and I found no error bars.
 quote: "DemyAgent-4B achieves state-of-the-art agentic reasoning performance, surpassing ReTool-32B (Feng et al., 2025) and rStar2-Agent-14B (Shang et al., 2025), and even outperforming Long-CoT models like DeepSeek-R1-Zero on AIME2025." (p.14)
 where: Table 2, p.15
2. Real end-to-end tool trajectories give a far better SFT start than ReTool-style stitched synthetic ones.
 number: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 AIME24 average@32 4.38% -> 33.23%; AIME25 3.65% -> 29.79%; pass@32 (AIME25) 22.22% -> 72.88%
 setup: SFT on both data types under identical settings, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B. The real set is 3k trajectories (teacher Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, Qwen-Agent, SandboxFusion; 1k LeetCode + 1k ReTool filtered by ReasonFlux-PRM, plus s1-1k). The 7B gains are smaller: AIME24 6.77 -> 17.91.
 quote: "the synthetic baseline yields below 10% on average@32 with unstable performance and a significantly lower ability upper bound." (p.5)
 where: Table 1, p.5
 note: the text says 29.97% / 45.22% for AIME25 while Table 1 shows 29.79% / 45.82%. This is an internal inconsistency.
3. Clip-higher plus overlong reward shaping (GRPO-TCR) beats the GRPO-T baseline on compute.
 number: Qwen3-4B: TCR 70.93%/68.13% (AIME24/25) average@32 within 450 steps; GRPO-T best 54.7%/40.93%, which TCR reaches in 100 steps (25% of compute)
 setup: GRPO-TCR = token-level loss + clip higher (eps_high 0.28, eps_low 0.20) + overlong shaping; GRPO-T = token-level, eps 0.2, reward r_out+tool, KL beta 0.001. The change from GRPO-T to TCR bundles two techniques, so clip-higher and shaping are not isolated from each other.
 quote: "GRPO-T only achieves the best average@32 performance of 54.7%/ 40.93% on AIME2024/AIME2025, which GRPO-TCR could achieve within only 100 training steps, utilizing only 25% of the training computation of GRPO-T." (p.7)
 where: Sec 4.1, p.7
4. Token-level loss beats sequence-level loss only for the stronger model.
 number: +3.95% on AIME24, +3.86% on AIME25 (Qwen3-4B); about equal for Qwen2.5-7B
 setup: GRPO-SCR uses eps_high 0.0004 / eps_low 0.0003 (very different clip values from TCR, which confounds the loss-granularity comparison)
 quote: "token-level loss exceeds sequence-level loss by 3.95% on AIME24 and 3.86% on AIME25 under the same training budget." (p.8)
 where: p.8
5. Diverse RL data raises entropy and speeds learning.
 number: over 50% average@32 on AIME25 in 150 steps vs 220 steps for the DAPO-Math-17k baseline
 setup: GRPO-TCR; 30k set = 17k DAPO-Math + 4,902 math and 3,586 code from Skywork-or1 + 3k science from MegaScience
 quote: "the agent achieves over 50% average@32 accuracy on AIME2025 within only 150 steps, while the DAPO-Math baseline requires 220 steps to reach the same level." (p.6)
 where: p.6, Fig 2
6. Model-aware data filtering rescues a weak model.
 number: none beyond the difficulty cutoffs: 8 rollouts per problem, drop 0% and 100% accuracy, easy >=0.75, hard <=0.25
 setup: Qwen2.5-7B-RA-SFT's average reward stagnated near zero on the full 30k set. The model-aware set matched the Qwen3 difficulty histogram. The gain is shown only as curves (Fig 3).
 where: Sec 3.3, p.6
7. A higher clip upper bound helps up to a point, then hurts.
 number: eps_high 0.28 -> 0.315 gives the same result at step 60 instead of step 100 ("40% faster"); 0.35 was worse on Qwen3-4B
 setup: eps_high in {0.28, 0.315, 0.35}, GRPO-TCR, both models. Weaker models want larger bounds, stronger ones tighter.
 quote: "with epsilon_high = 0.315, we achieve equivalent performance 40% faster, reaching the same results at step 60 that would otherwise require 100 steps" (paraphrase of p.10; the extraction renders the symbols differently)
 where: Sec 4.3, p.10
8. Agentic RL can raise pass@k and average@k together, unlike conventional RL, but only with the TCR/SCR recipes. GRPO-T showed the conventional trade-off and early entropy collapse.
 number: "over 10% gains" on both metrics on AIME24/25
 where: Sec 4.2, p.9
9. Deliberative mode (longer thinking, fewer tool calls) beats reactive mode (short thinking, many calls).
 number: deliberative agents have "over 70% success in tool usage"
 where: Sec 5.1, p.11-12, Fig 7-8. This is a correlation across runs, not a controlled intervention.
10. Long-CoT models (Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507) learn to avoid the tool.
 number: tool calls converge to zero in training
 setup: GRPO-TCR on reasoning-heavy tasks. SFT on the 3k tool data restores tool use, but the model ends up only comparable to instruct-based models. The authors argue the instruct models are the better start.
 where: Sec 5.2-5.3, p.12-14

Reward (Eq. 8): outcome + tool bonus, +1+0.1n if the answer matches, else -1+0.1n. The "min" in the extraction is garbled. The paper says the bonus is "clipped to avoid tool abuse", but the formula as printed shows no cap. Overlong shaping (Eq. 9): 0 within budget, linear penalty in the last L_cache tokens, -1 beyond L_max.

TRAINING SETUP (App A, p.22): VeRL; 8x A100-80G; SFT 5 epochs, batch 32, lr 5e-5; RL 3 epochs, batch 64, lr 1e-6, max prompt 2560, max response 16384; metrics average@32, pass@32, maj@32 (LCB pass@1/pass@5).

LIMITS
- Authors concede (Sec 9): only 4B/7B models; larger models may behave differently, with different sensitivities to reward and exploration; broader agentic settings are left for later.
- Sec 8.3: only a single static tool (code interpreter) was studied, and the insights are not tested on multi-tool or search settings.
- The paper does not show seeds, variance or significance. Many results are single-run curves. The clip-higher and reward-shaping ablations are bundled together. The loss-granularity comparison is confounded by different clip values. The eps_high sweep uses only three values. The benchmarks are math/science/code (AIME, GPQA, LCB). No tool-calling API or function-calling evaluation (BFCL, tau-bench) is done, and no web agents.
- The SFT teacher is Qwen3-Coder-30B, so the "real vs synthetic" comparison may also reflect distillation from a stronger model.
- The RL set contains DAPO-Math and the eval is AIME. The paper does not discuss contamination.

BUILDS ON: GRPO (Shao et al., 2024); DAPO clip-higher and overlong shaping (Yu et al., 2025); GSPO sequence-level loss (Zheng et al., 2025); ReTool (Feng et al., 2025, source of the synthetic SFT data and reward idea); entropy-collapse work (Cui et al., 2025); ARPO (Dong et al., 2025b); ToRL (Li et al., 2025d); rStar2-Agent (Shang et al., 2025).

CODE: none.

FIGURES (captions only; I did not render any): Fig 2 (diverse vs math-only RL data, AIME25 accuracy and entropy, p.6); Fig 3 (30k vs model-aware data, p.7); Fig 4 (T/TCR/SCR on AIME, p.8); Fig 5 (entropy, p.10); Fig 6 (eps_high sweep, p.10); Fig 7-8 (tool calls, response length, tool-use efficiency, p.11-12); Fig 9-10 (Long-CoT vs instruct, p.13-14).

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean apart from garbled math symbols. No embedded instructions. Seeds and run counts are not reported. The text-vs-table mismatch is in claim 2.

VERBATIM QUOTES FOR THE NOTE
- "Agentic RL requires balanced policy entropy, which avoids both excessive entropy (instability) and insufficient entropy (premature convergence) for optimal training effectiveness." (Takeaway 4.3, p.11)
- "Current open-source Long-CoT LLMs optimized for reasoning tasks cannot be directly applied in Agentic RL, since they over-rely on internal reasoning and avoid invoking tools when encountering reasoning tasks." (Takeaway 5.2, p.13)
- "our experiments are conducted on small-sized models (e.g, 4B/7B)." (Sec 9, p.17)
